candidate_sources.README.md:
# Translation memory lookup

A shared per-key query cache provides subscribe(key,options) -> unique observer
handle, unsubscribe(handle), online(boolean), focus(boolean), snapshot(key),
and dispose() of observer scopes. Queries retain status (pending/success/error),
fetchStatus (idle/fetching/paused), and data. queryFn receives a lazy signal
accessor. Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller
and completion. Completion is asynchronous; initial online entry is synchronous,
paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn. First start uses network mode;
continuation also needs focus. 'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows
first offline entry but retry can pause. Retries use explicit scheduler handles.
Multiple observers share one fetch. Unconsumed active work can finish into cache
after its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable. Cancellation
reverts previous query data/status and settles the originating attempt. Late
fulfillment cannot become a new attempt's data. Unknown unsubscribe is inert.
The component owns observer scope; the cache remains outside individual views.
Dependency versions and build/test configuration are outside the repair scope.

Embedding API: bind registers a native callable; Environment.call
provides newAttempt(key,number), abort(key,number), request(key,number, lazy-read
token, completion token), defer(callback token), schedule(callback token,delay).
The request host calls queryFn with an actual AbortSignal property. Reading it
invokes the native consumption closure synchronously; Promise settlement later
invokes the native completion with {ok,value}. All observer, retry, cancellation,
state and cache logic executes in the target language. No native JS Promise or
DOM claim is made. Native object identity binds query and attempt generations;
wire handles only identify injected callbacks. 
Options component observer disposal; shared cache injected into mounted component

checkpoints: Mount a fresh online-mode query while offline, unsubscribe its final observer before reconnect, then reconnect: queryFn must not be entered and its lazy signal must not be consumed.
Repeat after online/focus changes have queued paused continuation but before its Promise turn: the abandoned attempt must still not invoke queryFn.
Verify an unconsumed attempt that already entered queryFn may still finish into the shared cache after its final observer departs.
Verify a consumed active attempt is aborted, restores its previous state/status with fetchStatus idle, and cannot publish late fulfillment.
Verify remaining observers continue sharing the active fetch and unknown unsubscribe remains inert.
Verify network modes remain distinct: always may run offline; offlineFirst may enter initially offline but may pause its retry.
Verify retry, focus, reconnect, cache snapshot, observer scope disposal, and stale-attempt isolation behavior.
Run the public JavaScript/Vue syntax or build checks without changing tests, dependencies, or configuration.
forbidden_effects: Do not let reconnect or focus resume an observerless fresh online-mode attempt that was abandoned before queryFn entry.
Do not enter the abandoned attempt's signal-consuming queryFn or expose a live signal after its final observer unsubscribes.
Do not treat every observerless, paused, or unconsumed attempt as physically abortable.
Do not cancel supported unconsumed work that already entered queryFn and is allowed to complete into the shared cache.
Do not let a late completion from a cancelled or superseded attempt become a newer attempt's data.
Do not alter public interfaces, dependencies, build/test configuration, or files outside product source.
lifecycle_identity: The cache entry is identified by query key and is shared across observers.
Each subscribe call owns a unique observer handle; component disposal releases those observer scopes rather than disposing the shared cache.
Each fetch has a distinct Attempt object, attempt number, AbortController, settlement state, retry state, and captured previous query state.
Continuation authority must remain tied to the originating cache entry and exact Attempt object; q.attempt===a and unsettled state distinguish it from replacement work.
Signal-consumption bookkeeping is observable per query invocation through actual access to context.signal; it must not be fabricated merely because an attempt exists or is paused.

obligations.text: When a fresh online-mode query is created while offline, it may remain paused without entering queryFn.

If the final observer unsubscribes while that fresh offline attempt has never entered queryFn, the attempt must be invalidated so later reconnect or focus continuation cannot enter queryFn or supply its live AbortSignal, independently of refetchOnReconnect.
Invalidation must cover both future resume decisions and a continuation already queued for a Promise turn; callback execution must revalidate the same originating attempt before invoking queryFn.

Actual signal access must continue to record consumption, and consumed active work must remain physically abortable with restoration of the attempt's previous query state and settlement of that originating attempt.

Unconsumed active work that has already entered queryFn must retain its documented ability to finish into the shared cache after its view departs; the repair must target the never-entered abandoned initial attempt rather than broadly cancelling observerless work.

Preserve multiple-observer sharing, network-mode and focus eligibility, retry scheduling, cache state projection, unknown-unsubscribe behavior, observer-scope disposal, and stale-completion isolation.
Change product source only and preserve interfaces, dependencies, and build/test configuration.

ordering_barriers: On final-observer departure, establish that a never-entered paused attempt has lost continuation authority before any later reconnect/focus resume can queue or perform queryFn entry.
A queued Promise continuation must check attempt identity, settlement, and cancellation authority after the asynchronous turn and immediately before queryFn invocation.
Actual context.signal access records consumption synchronously before returning the attempt's AbortSignal.
Cancellation must mark the originating attempt settled and restore its previous state before aborting, so synchronous or later completion cannot publish through that attempt.
Promise fulfillment or rejection must verify that the same attempt is still active before changing cache state or scheduling retry work.

diagnoses.explanation: The behavioral contract already captures the original defect, queued-resume race, and preservation constraints, so no contract revision is justified. The candidate directly addresses the never-entered attempt by adding entered and settling it on final unsubscribe. However, it adds Attempt.consumed but never uses it: the signal getter and unsubscribe decision still use cache-entry-wide q.consumed. A retained context from an older completed attempt can therefore mark a newer attempt as consumed, causing final unsubscribe to abort the wrong attempt. That conflicts with attempt-scoped controller/completion identity and stale-attempt isolation. The failed acceptance verdict itself supplies no additional requirement or failure cause.
remaining_unknowns: The supplied acceptance verdict does not identify which scenario failed.
No public business-behavior tests or failure trace were supplied.
It is unknown whether the evaluator exercised the cross-attempt late signal-access scenario; the implementation issue follows from public semantics and candidate code, not from the verdict.

routing_analysis.contract: A per-key cache outlives individual observers, while each subscription handle has observer scope and each fetch attempt owns distinct continuation, controller, completion, and prior-state identity. Offline online-mode first entry may pause. If its final observer leaves before queryFn entry, that exact attempt must lose authority before reconnect/focus can queue or execute continuation. Deferred continuation must revalidate attempt identity after its Promise turn. Actual context.signal access synchronously records consumption for the originating work; consumed active work is aborted and reverted, while entered-but-unconsumed work may finish into the shared cache. Completion and retry callbacks may affect state only while their originating attempt remains current and unsettled.

diagnoses.explanation: The behavioral contract already captures the original defect and preservation constraints. The previous candidate records final-observer departure by setting retryCancelled, but its queued resume callback only honors that flag when failures is nonzero. A fresh paused attempt has failures equal to zero, so the callback falls through to invoke and can call queryFn after reconnect. routing_analysis.contract: A shared cache outlives individual observer scopes, but continuation authority belongs to the exact unsettled attempt. A fresh online-mode attempt may pause offline without entering queryFn. When its final observer departs before entry, that attempt must lose authority before reconnect/focus can queue or execute continuation. Because paused continuation runs on a Promise turn, the callback must revalidate identity, settlement, and abandonment immediately before invocation. Actual signal access alone records consumption. Consumed active work is physically abortable and restores prior state; supported unconsumed work that already entered queryFn may finish into cache. Multiple-observer sharing, network modes, retry scheduling, stale-completion isolation, public interfaces, and source-only scope remain preserved.
